en: The Apadāna of the Elder Revata of the Acacia Forest Buddhavagga 11. Khadiravaniyarevatattheraapadāna
“The Ganges, named Bhāgīrathī,
flows forth from the Himalayas;
at a certain ford, I was a boatman.”
And I crossed over that very flood.
Padumuttara, the Leader,
the Fully Enlightened One, the supreme among bipeds;
Accompanied by hundreds of thousands,
he arrived at the bank of the Ganges;
having brought together many boats, he [proceeded].
Having had a covering made for the ship by skilled craftsmen,
I honored the Bull among Men.
And having arrived, the Sambuddha boarded that boat;
standing in the midst of the water, the Teacher—
He spoke these verses:
“He who ferried across the Fully Awakened One and the untainted Saṅgha as well;”
Through that clarity of mind,
you will delight in the world of the gods;
you will be reborn in a celestial mansion.
Well-fashioned and not resting on any support,
it will always hold a canopy of flowers suspended in the sky.
In the fifty-eighth aeon,
there was a kshatriya named Tāraka,
a conqueror of the four quarters.
He will become a wheel-turning monarch.
In the fifty-seventh aeon,
there will be a kṣatriya named Cammaka;
Like the sun rising,
he of great power will shine forth after a hundred thousand eons.
Born of the Okkāka clan,
he will be a teacher in the world named Gotama by lineage.
Having passed away from the Tidasas,
he will go to the human state;
he will be known by the name Revata.
He will become a mere kinsman of Brahmins.
Having gone forth from the household life,
impelled by his white roots of merit;
He will go forth in the teaching of the Blessed One Gotama;
having gone forth later, he—
One who is devoted to yoga and practices insight,
having fully understood all taints,
will attain Nibbāna, free from taints.
Energy is my yoke-bearing ox,
carrying me toward security from bondage;
I bear this final body.
In the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
the karma performed during one hundred thousand [aeons] has shown its fruit here to me.
Like the speed of an arrow released,
he burned away my defilements; then, as I was dwelling in the forest, he [spoke] to me.
Having seen this, the Sage who has reached the end of the world designated the forest-dwelling bhikkhus as foremost,
O Great-minded One.
The four analytical knowledges and these eight liberations have been realized,
along with the six direct knowledges.
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the Venerable Elder Revata of the Acacia Grove recited these verses.
This is the ninth legend (apadāna) of the Elder Revata of the Acacia Grove.
